applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Spain-Mexico Double Taxation Agreement (1992, as amended)
Spain-Argentina Double Taxation Agreement (1978, as amended)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Ley 10/2010, de 28 de abril, de prevención del blanqueo de capitales y de la financiación del terrorismo, as amended by Ley 6/2023, de 17 de marzo, regulating the Registro Central de Titularidades Reales; Real Decreto 304/2014, de 5 de mayo, implementing the prudential requirements; Real Decreto 190/2018, de 23 de marzo, amending the UBO identification and filing duties.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificación Negativa de Denominación (Negative Name Certificate)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Online issuance through the registered electronic signature system, no apostille required

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarial Power of Attorney for incorporation granted by each non-resident shareholder or director
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary Public in the country of origin (or Spanish Consulate)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (Spain is party to the 1961 Hague Apostille Convention)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing / Certificate of Legal Existence of any corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate Registry of the shareholder's country of incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille and certified Spanish translation by a sworn translator

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Capital Deposit Certificate (Certificado de Desembolso) evidencing payment of the initial share capital
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Spanish credit institution or payment account provider
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Private document issued by the bank; must be presented to the notary at signing

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all directors, shareholders holding more than 25%, and beneficial owners against Spain's domestic PEP database, the EU consolidated sanctions list, UN Security Council consolidated list, and OFAC SDN list. The obliged entity (lawyer or incorporation agent) must apply risk-based due diligence, identify the source of funds, and complete the Declaración de Titularidad Real (UBO declaration) in the Central Registry under Law 6/2023. Any hit triggers a Suspicious Transaction Report to SEPBLAC (Servicio Ejecutivo de la Comisión de Prevención del Blanqueo de Capitales y Obligaciones) and a moratorium on incorporation.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Mercantil Central (Central Commercial Registry) online name clearance service — https://www.registradores.org; electronic incorporation also available via CIRCE (Centro de Información y Red de Creación de Empresas) at https://www.circe.es
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company denominations must be expressed in Spanish or in any co-official language of the Spanish State (Catalan, Basque, Galician). Names originally in foreign languages must be transliterated into the Latin alphabet; non-Latin scripts are not admissible. The name must include the suffix 'Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada' or the abbreviation 'S.L.' as a separate token at the end of the denomination. Denomination must not be identical or confusingly similar to any existing company name in the Central Registry.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the application for a negative name certificate is rejected, the applicant or its legal representative may (i) submit a new name application using a different proposed denomination, or (ii) file an administrative appeal (recurso de alzada) within one month of the rejection notice before the Dirección General de Seguridad Jurídica y Fe Pública (DGSJFP) under Ley 39/2015, of 1 October, on Common Administrative Procedure. The appeal must state the grounds of non-confusion and can attach comparative registry evidence. No extension of the 90-day name reservation is permitted; after expiry, a fresh application must be filed.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office or digital co-working address may be used as the registered office for a low-risk POD retail SL, provided it comprises a physical Turkish address (not a PO Box) in a Spanish municipality, permits acceptance of official notifications, and is designated in the deed of incorporation. Spanish courts and tax agencies may disregard a purely nominal address if no commercial substance or reception capacity exists, so the virtual office must include mail handling and lease or service contract documentation.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Negative Name Certificate (Certificación Negativa de Denominación) application and issuance fee
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Registro Mercantil Central / Colegio de Registradores de España
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff under Real Decreto 1427/1989 and the Registradores pricing schedule (current fee range €10–€30)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Public deed of incorporation (Escritura de Constitución) executed before a Spanish notary
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Notary Public (Notaría) appointed by the incorporation agent
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Notarial tariff (arancel notarial) regulated by Real Decreto 1426/1989, as amended; market benchmark for a single-member SL between €180–€500

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Commercial Registry filing and inscription fee (Registro Mercantil)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Registry tariff under Real Decreto 1427/1989 and accounting volume supplemental fees; typical SL inscription €50–€120

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered office address service (virtual office with mail handling) — first year
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Private virtual office provider / legal representative
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for a Madrid or Barcelona virtual office, including notification acceptance and client meeting hours

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Apostille, legalization, and sworn translation of shareholder and director documents
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Competent authorities in country of origin (e.g., Ministry of Foreign Affairs) and Spanish sworn translators
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Hague Convention fixed fees plus translator tariff of roughly $50–$100 per document

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Tax identification number (NIF provisional) solicitation and communication to tax authorities
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Free of charge; statutory procedure under Real Decreto 1065/2007

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Spanish Royal Legislative Decree 1/2010 of 2 July, approving the consolidated text of the Capital Companies Act (Ley de Sociedades de Capital), as amended by Law 15/2022 and Law 18/2022; applicable Articles 4(2), 20-22, 58, 60, 174-179 and transitory provisions on Sociedad Limitada de Formación Sucesiva.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registro Mercantil Central for name certification; Registro Mercantil Provincial of the province of the registered office for incorporation registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Public deed of incorporation (escritura de constitución) submitted for registration in the Registro Mercantil, together with de forma complementaria Form 036/037 where required.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: SL may be incorporated with share capital of EUR 1 or more; if capital below EUR 3,000, the Sociedad Limitada de Formación Sucesiva (SLFS) regime applies, obliging the company to allocate 20% of annual profits to a legal reserve until EUR 3,000 is accumulated and to restrict certain distributions. If capital equals or exceeds EUR 3,000, the full amount must be subscribed and paid-up at grant, evidenced by a bank capital-deposit certificate. No formal escrow account is prescribed; the deposited funds remain blocked until company registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: The directors, duly convened, resolved: 1. To accept the subscription and payment of the share capital represented in the incorporation deed, approving the provisional bank-ready statement of the subscribed units and confirming all capital obligations are satisfied under the SLFS/standard SL regime. 2. To adopt as the statutory registered office the address recited in Article 4 of the bylaws, to authorize the notarization and presentation of the deed before the Mercantile Registry. 3. To appoint [Name] as sole administrator with all powers, accepting the written acceptance. 4. To execute all ancillary forms, including the acquisition of NIF and registration in the social security system, and to open online market payment accounts (Stripe, PayPal).

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the official name-certification application (solicitud de certificación de denominación social) through the Registro Mercantil Central online portal, proposing at least three company names in order of preference and providing the promoters' identification data. The registry certifies that the selected name is not identical or sufficiently similar to any existing corporation and issues an exclusive negative-name certificate valid for three months.
required_dossiers: Signed application for denominación social / name certificate
Passport or NIE of each founding member
Power of representation if acting through an agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the first preferred name is rejected because it coincides with an existing entity, the examiner assesses the next preferred name; if all names are rejected, submit a new application with alternate names.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Apply for provisional NIF of the company in formation
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the censual declaration (Form 036) at the provincial AEAT office, requesting a provisional corporate NIF for the company in formation, attaching the negative name certificate and identifying the legal representative. The tax office assigns the provisional NIF before execution of the deed, enabling the opening of the bank capital account and notarization.
required_dossiers: Signed Form 036
Negative name certificate issued by Registro Mercantil Central
Passport or NIE of the representative and promoters
Evidence of the intended registered address and business activity
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the census form is rejected for inconsistent data, correct the form and refile; if the tax authority requests additional identification, provide a notarized power of representation and updated identity documents.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Subscribe and pay up share capital through a bank deposit certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Credit institution established and authorized in Spain
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary restricted account in the name of 'ES_SL en formación' using the provisional NIF, deposit the subscribed share capital (any amount above EUR 1, with EUR 3,000 required for the standard SL regime), and obtain an official capital-deposit certificate. No formal escrow is required; funds remain blocked until the company is registered and the certificate is delivered to the notary.
required_dossiers: Provisional NIF certificate from AEAT
Negative name certificate
Passport or NIE of each subscriber
AML declaration of source of funds where the deposit exceeds EUR 10,000
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank applies enhanced due diligence, supply a simple corporate ownership diagram and tax residence declaration; unresolved AML queries may be cured by obtaining a notarized pecuniary certification of capital instead of a bank certificate.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execute public deed and register the company in the Mercantile Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Present to the notary the negative name certificate, provisional NIF, capital-deposit certificate, draft bylaws and identity documents of the subscribers and proposed administrator. The notary verifies legal capacity, reads the bylaws, and grants the public incorporation deed. Within one month, submit the deed, Form 036/census data and identification copies to the provincial Mercantile Registry, which examines legality and enters the company in the Register.
required_dossiers: Negative name certificate valid at notary date
Provisional NIF of the company in formation
Bank capital deposit certificate
Draft bylaws conforming to Articles 20-30 of the Capital Companies Act
Passport or NIE of founding members
Criminal record certificate of each proposed administrator
Written acceptance of office by the appointed administrators
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registrar issues a defect (nota de calificación), remedy each defect by a notarial amendment or by supplying the missing document, then re-present the deed; if the defect concerns insufficient capital, amend the bylaws and increase or complete the capital contribution.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Complete post-registration tax, social security, municipal and e-payment setup
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: AEAT, Tesorería General de la Seguridad Social (TGSS) and local city council through the Ventanilla Única Empresarial
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After registration, file Form 036/037 to convert the provisional NIF into a definitive CIF/NIF, register the company and its directors/employees for social security, and obtain the municipal opening license (licencia de apertura or declaración responsable) for the POD warehouse and light-print facility. Finally, submit the registered deed, definitive NIF, company information and director identification to Stripe and PayPal for onboarding of the e-commerce payment accounts.
required_dossiers: Registered incorporation deed (inscripción del Registro Mercantil)
Definitive CIF/NIF certificate from AEAT
Completed Form 036/037 and business commencement data
Lease contract or title documenting use of the physical premises
Statement of responsible activity and fire-safety certificate
Occupational risk prevention assessment
AML/KYB package for PSA payment-provider onboarding
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the municipal license application is challenged, submit a technical report by an architect and adjust the activity classification; where local rules permit, convert the license procedure into a declaración responsable for low-risk retail to continue operations pending resolution.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Dirección General de Industria, Pyme y Comercio (Regional Authority) and local Municipal Licensing Department acting through the Ventanilla Única Empresarial
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Licencia Municipal de Apertura y Actividad (or Declaración Responsable de Inicio de Actividad for low-risk premises)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministerio para la Transición Ecológica y el Reto Demográfico and the corresponding regional environmental consejería
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category IV - Exempt from full EIA for low-impact retail and small digital-printing installations; mandatory registration as a producer of non-municipal residues and submission of a minimal environmental startup communication where solvent/IR consumption exceeds small-emitter thresholds.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater below 2 m3/day to municipal sewer must comply with the local sewer ordinance, including suspended solids below 300 mg/L and COD below 600 mg/L; VOC emissions from digital printing must remain below the applicable small-emitter threshold (e.g., solvent consumption below 0.6 kg/h or aggregate annual consumption under 1.5 t/y) consistent with EU Directive 2010/75/EU and national transposition; residual toners, ink cartridges, and contaminated rags must be traceable to a registered waste manager.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire Safety Certificate (certificado de protección contra incendios) evidencing extinguishers, evacuation signage, and the building occupancy classification; structural certificate for storage racks and mezzanine loads; and the mandatory occupational risk assessment under Ley 31/1995, together with first-aid equipment and the corresponding communication of the workplace to the labor authority.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT); electronic portal: Sede Electrónica de la AEAT (sede.agenciatributaria.gob.es)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: At formation, the notary obtains a provisional corporate NIF (Número de Identificación Fiscal) electronically from AEAT before executing the public deed of incorporation. After definitive registration with the Registro Mercantil (within one month), the SL must file Form 036 (Declaración Censal) electronically at the Sede Electrónica to obtain the definitive NIF, register in the IAE census, and open the IVA registry (Censo de Obligados Tributarios). A qualified digital certificate (FNMT Certificado de Persona Jurídica or registered-e-signature) is required for all filings. Non-resident shareholders/parent entities must obtain a non-resident NIF through a Spanish tax representative (representante fiscal) using Form 036/016; the Spanish SL reports their participation on annual filings. Definitive NIF is issued within 1-5 business days, subject to registry verification, and IVA registration is effective from the date of commencement of taxable activities.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation: The SL is a Spanish tax resident (managed and controlled in Spain) subject to Impuesto sobre Sociedades (Law 27/2014) at the standard 25% rate on worldwide income. No pass-through/transparency election exists; profits are taxed at entity level and distributions carry 19% dividend withholding (exempt or credit-relieved for EU resident corporate shareholders under the Parent-Subsidiary Directive). Territorial scope: worldwide taxation on accounting profit adjusted under LIS; profits of foreign permanent establishments may be exempt under Art. 22 LIS. Tax_Exempt_Zone: not applicable to mainland Spain; only the Canary Islands ZEC regime (authorized entities with Canary Islands HQ and employees) provides a reduced 4% rate.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Spain has no check-the-box or fiscal-transparency election. Available statutory options: (1) Grupo de Consolidación Fiscal (LIS Art. 55-75) for groups with ≥70% voting control, enabling joint IS filing; (2) ETVE international holding regime (Art. 21 LIS) providing full participation exemption for qualifying EU/non-EU shareholdings; (3) reduced 15% IS rate for newly created SLs in the first two taxable years with active business income (Art. 29.1 LIS); (4) accelerated depreciation and special SME rules (Art. 101-105 LIS) available when turnover < €10 million; (5) optional cash-basis VAT scheme (Régimen Especial del Criterio de Caja) for sellers with annual turnover ≤ €2 million; (6) mandatory ATAD hybrid-mismatch adjustments (Art. 15 septies LIS, Law 11/2021) with no election, including the switch-over rule for tax-transparent third-country entities.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: IVA (Impuesto sobre el Valor Añadido) - Value Added Tax
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Effective €0 - no general exemption threshold. Any entity (resident or non-resident) initiating taxable supplies in Spanish territory must register for IVA before commencing activity (LIVA Art. 164; RGAT Art. 17). Non-resident EU distance sellers to Spanish consumers may use the One Stop Shop (OSS) with a €10,000 EU-wide annual distance-sales threshold; non-EU sellers have no threshold and must register for IVA via a tax representative. Intra-EU acquisitions of goods by the SL are exempt from IVA up to €10,000 per calendar year (Art. 14 LIVA), but the option to apply IVA may be exercised.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Dual mandate effective 2025-2026: (a) Verifactu (Law 11/2021, RD 1007/2023) - from 1 July 2025, all billing software must be certified and generate tamper-proof XML invoice records with hash-chaining ('hash encadenado') and a Verifactu QR, made available to AEAT immediately upon request; (b) Law 18/2022 (Crea y Crece) - structured B2B e-invoicing (XML/UBL, not PDF) becomes mandatory for all entrepreneurs and companies, phased in 12 months (turnover > €8M) and 24 months after the implementing regulation is published, transacted via FACe/e.Factura or certified private operators; (c) SII real-time clearance - taxpayers in REDEME (monthly VAT refunds, including exporters under Art. 30 LIVA) and groups with annual turnover > €6M must transmit invoice records via the SII API to AEAT within 4 business days of issuance (8 for others), with mandatory validation codes and settlement mapping.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods: full exemption with credit (0% VAT) under Art. 21.1 LIVA where goods are exported outside EU customs territory by the supplier or on its behalf; export must be documented, transit must commence within 90 days of the taxable event, and evidence retained for 4 years. POD goods shipped by international courier qualify via the customs export declaration (DUA) or the electronic export data set (EXS/ICS) accompanying the parcel; low-value postal exports ≤ €150 may be exempt from duty and VAT. Services: exemption applies to services directly related to exported goods (Art. 21.8 and 19.1 LIVA) and to B2B services supplied to non-EU established customers under the place-of-supply rules (Art. 69 LIVA), effectively outside Spanish VAT (0%); proof of the customer's non-EU establishment (registry extract, non-EU VAT number, or passport/government ID) is required.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (DUA - Documento Único Administrativo) with customs office Electronic Export System (EXS) record of exit
Bill of Lading (B/L) or Air Waybill (AWB) / CMR consignment note evidencing EU exit
Commercial Invoice issued per Art. 6 Real Decreto 1619/2012, including Incoterms and export reference
Packing List detailing POD items and quantities
Proof of actual payment received: Inward Remittance Certificate, SWIFT MT103, or PSP settlement report (Stripe/PayPal) linked to the export invoice
Carrier tracking report showing physical exit from EU territory (for postal/courier low-value POD parcels)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: AEAT export-control audits under Art. 87.2 LIVA require a complete documentary chain for 4 years; failure reclassifies the transaction as a domestic supply taxed at 21% with late-payment interest (interés de demora). False zero-rating claims constitute a serious infraction (LGT Art. 194): penalty of 50%-100% of the understated IVA (15% reduction for voluntary correction) plus surcharges; customs-related false declarations carry additional penalties (LGT Art. 184-195). Criminal tax fraud under Organic Law 10/1995 Art. 305 applies when defrauded quota in any single tax year exceeds €120,000, with imprisonment of 1-5 years and fines of 2-6 times the defrauded amount. Non-repatriation of export proceeds within 180 days triggers Banco de España exchange-control violations (Art. 17-18 of Law 19/2003) with fines up to €30 million or 50% of the operation for serious cases. Retrospective clawback extends to the 4-year statute of limitations (suspended/extended on fraud), with digital SII/Verifactu analytics enabling automated risk scoring and cross-matching of customs, banking, and PSP settlement data.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banco de España, acting as the Spanish national competent authority within the Eurosystem, under the monetary policy framework of the European Central Bank. Foreign-exchange and capital-movement rules are principally derived from European Union law and Spanish Law 19/2003 on the legal regime of capital movements and foreign economic transactions. Banco de España and the Spanish Ministry of Economy, Trade and Enterprise administer applicable reporting and supervisory functions.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Spain uses the euro, which is fully convertible for current-account and capital-account transactions. There is no general Spanish exchange-control approval requirement for ordinary imports, exports, dividend payments, interest payments, intercompany settlements, capital contributions, shareholder loans, or repatriation of profits. Payments remain subject to bank anti-money-laundering, sanctions, beneficial-ownership, tax, and source-of-funds controls. Dividend and interest remittances must comply with Spanish corporate-law distribution rules, available distributable profits, solvency and reserve requirements, board and shareholder approvals, withholding-tax analysis, applicable tax treaties, and transfer-pricing requirements. Cross-border transactions may be reportable for balance-of-payments, statistical, tax, customs, or foreign-investment purposes. Transactions involving sanctioned jurisdictions, restricted counterparties, unusual payment chains, or high-risk jurisdictions may be delayed, rejected, or subject to enhanced due diligence.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Spain has no general statutory requirement for exporters to surrender export proceeds to a Spanish bank, convert foreign-currency receipts into euros, or comply with a mandatory conversion ratio. Export receipts may generally be retained in foreign-currency accounts or converted at the company's commercial discretion. The company must preserve commercial invoices, customs or intra-EU supply records, contracts, shipping evidence, payment evidence, and accounting records. Banks may request transaction-purpose and underlying-trade documentation. Applicable statistical, customs, VAT, Intrastat, tax, and bank-reporting obligations are separate from currency-conversion requirements. Large or unusual cross-border transactions may trigger information requests under Spanish financial and AML rules.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account; capital-contribution or share-capital funding account subject to bank acceptance and corporate-registration documentation
Operational Account; capital-contribution or share-capital funding account subject to bank acceptance and corporate-registration documentation
Operational Account; capital-contribution or share-capital funding account subject to bank acceptance and corporate-registration documentation
Operational Account; capital-contribution or share-capital funding account subject to bank acceptance and corporate-registration documentation

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium for payment collection and routine commercial payments; low as the sole treasury bank for an SL with non-resident ownership, material cross-border flows, foreign-currency exposure, or capital-injection requirements. An EU-authorised electronic-money institution or payment institution may provide payment accounts, merchant acquiring, cards, and certain cross-border transfers, but it is not equivalent to a Spanish bank deposit account and client funds are generally safeguarded rather than covered as bank deposits by the Deposit Guarantee Scheme. The provider must be authorised in its EEA home state and validly passported or otherwise permitted to provide services in Spain. Offshore digital EMIs without EU authorisation, appropriate passporting, or a compliant local service model should not be used for regulated payment services. EMI onboarding does not eliminate Spanish corporate, tax, AML, sanctions, accounting, or beneficial-ownership obligations. Stripe and PayPal should be treated as payment-collection providers, not substitutes for the company's principal operating and reserve bank account.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Spanish law does not impose a universal requirement that all directors physically attend a branch to open a corporate account. Remote onboarding may be available where the bank accepts reliable electronic identification, qualified signatures, video identification, documentary verification, and beneficial-owner verification. The bank may nevertheless require a branch meeting, live video interview, notarised or apostilled documents, Spanish sworn translations, certified copies, or an in-person appearance by an authorised signatory. Non-resident directors, complex ownership chains, nominee arrangements, high-risk countries, cash-intensive activity, inconsistent business explanations, or foreign-source funding materially increase the likelihood of enhanced due diligence and physical-interview requirements.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear ultimate beneficial ownership, layered non-resident ownership, nominee shareholders, or mismatch between the shareholder register, corporate filings, and onboarding declarations
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Current articles of association; deed of incorporation and subsequent amendments; commercial-register extract or equivalent official certificates; complete ownership chart through natural persons; UBO identification and address evidence; director and authorised-signatory IDs; beneficial-ownership declaration; shareholder register; powers of attorney; and certified translations or apostilles where requested.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unexplained inbound capital, shareholder loans, or transfers from an account held by a person other than the registered shareholder or lender
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed capital-increase resolution or shareholder funding agreement; shareholder-loan agreement where applicable; bank statements showing origin of funds; source-of-wealth and source-of-funds evidence; tax and financial statements of the funding party; board or shareholder approvals; payment instruction identifying the legal purpose; and evidence that the remitter is the shareholder, lender, or an authorised regulated intermediary.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Business model perceived as inconsistent with a low-risk print-on-demand retail classification, including high-volume refunds, marketplace flows, prepaid balances, virtual assets, cash, or unexplained third-party payments
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Detailed business plan; website and storefront URLs; product catalogue; supplier and fulfilment contracts; customer geography; order-flow diagram; payment-provider agreements; expected monthly transaction volumes and average ticket size; refund and chargeback policy; logistics evidence; sample invoices; VAT registration information; and written confirmation that the company does not handle cash, virtual assets, or customer funds as a regulated service.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Payments involving high-risk jurisdictions, sanctioned countries, sanctioned persons, politically exposed persons, or counterparties whose names generate sanctions-screening alerts
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Counterparty legal-name and ownership verification; sanctions-screening results; contracts and invoices; shipping and customs documentation; end-use and end-user statements; beneficial-owner certificates; screening logs; compliance policy; and a written explanation demonstrating that the transaction is lawful and unrelated to sanctioned activity. No payment should proceed until the bank clears the alert.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Insufficient Spanish tax and corporate substance for the stated activity, including no registered office evidence, no operational explanation, or unexplained reliance on foreign payment accounts
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Spanish registered-office evidence; lease or service agreement; tax identification number; commercial-register records; accounting and tax-adviser engagement; employment or contractor arrangements where applicable; fulfilment and supplier agreements; management-responsibility matrix; expected Spanish and foreign revenue split; and a treasury policy explaining the role of each bank and payment provider.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inconsistent transaction profile, rapid movement of funds, circular transfers, frequent unrelated third-party receipts, or payments lacking invoices and commercial rationale
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Rolling cash-flow forecast; transaction-monitoring reconciliation; invoice and purchase-order archive; customer and supplier master data; payment-purpose coding; bank reconciliation policy; segregation-of-duties matrix; transfer-pricing documentation for related-party flows; and management certification explaining exceptional transactions.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Document deficiencies, expired identification, uncertified foreign corporate documents, unreliable electronic signatures, or inability to verify foreign directors and UBOs
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Recently issued official certificates; valid passports or national identity documents; proof of residential address; apostille or legalisation where required; sworn Spanish translations where requested; qualified electronic signatures; notarised powers of attorney; and a controlled document register tracking validity and renewal dates.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Route shareholder capital contributions, share-capital subscriptions, share-premium funding, or shareholder loans from an account held in the verified name of the shareholder or lender to the Spanish SL's bank account. Use SEPA Credit Transfer for euro payments where available and SWIFT MT103 for non-SEPA or foreign-currency payments. State a precise payment purpose such as share-capital subscription, share premium, capital contribution, or shareholder loan and include the legal entity name and tax identification number. Before funding, provide the bank with the incorporation deed, current corporate-register extract, ownership and UBO chart, board or shareholder resolution, funding agreement, source-of-funds evidence, and expected transaction profile. Reconcile the incoming payment to the accounting entry and retain the payment confirmation. For a formal capital increase, coordinate the notarial deed, Commercial Registry filing, accounting treatment, and bank evidence required by the notary or bank. Do not split transfers to avoid controls, use unrelated third-party remitters, or route funds through an offshore EMI without a documented legal and commercial rationale.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Use SEPA Credit Transfer or SEPA Instant Credit Transfer for eligible euro suppliers and SWIFT MT103 for non-SEPA payments. For recurring print-on-demand suppliers, obtain verified beneficiary details, execute supplier contracts, retain purchase orders, commercial invoices, delivery or fulfilment evidence, and reconcile payments to inventory or cost-of-sales records. For higher-value, new, or higher-risk suppliers, use a documentary Commercial Letter of Credit, preferably an irrevocable and, where commercially justified, confirmed LC, subject to UCP 600 and applicable bank procedures. Documentary collections may use URC 522 where appropriate. Payment instructions should identify the invoice, contract, goods or services, beneficiary, country, and purpose. Apply dual approval, beneficiary-change call-back controls, sanctions screening, and segregation of duties. For imports from outside the European Union, align payment records with customs declarations, import VAT, tariff records, and transport documentation. For intra-EU purchases, preserve VAT identification, dispatch, and acquisition evidence.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable forward foreign-exchange contracts with an authorised bank or regulated investment firm, used to hedge documented forecast or committed payables and receivables and supported by an internal hedging policy.

Non-deliverable forwards, where legally and commercially available through an authorised counterparty, generally settled in cash against an agreed reference rate and subject to suitability, documentation, collateral, and reporting requirements.

Currency swaps or cross-currency swaps with an authorised bank for documented funding or currency-mismatch exposure, subject to ISDA or equivalent master documentation, collateral terms, valuation controls, and counterparty limits.
Spot foreign-exchange transactions through the operating bank for ordinary settlement and treasury conversion needs.

Currency options or collars may be considered only after separate suitability, cost, accounting, valuation, and counterparty review; speculative trading unrelated to the company's commercial exposure should be prohibited.

Hedging counterparties should be EU-regulated banks or appropriately authorised investment firms. The company should document the hedged item, notional, tenor, currency, valuation, accounting treatment, counterparty approval, collateral requirements, and termination rights. Derivatives may trigger EMIR reporting, clearing, margin, risk-mitigation, and record-keeping obligations depending on the instrument, counterparties, and transaction classification.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Accounts Deposit (Depósito de Cuentas Anuales): Balance Sheet, Profit & Loss Account, Statement of Changes in Equity, and Annex in mandatory digital XBRL format, filed with the Mercantile Registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registro Mercantil de la provincia del domicilio social (Spanish Mercantile Registry); publication of the deposit notice in BORME (Official Mercantile Registry Gazette)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Shareholders' meeting (Junta General) must approve the annual accounts within 6 months of fiscal year-end (30 June for calendar-year filers); the approved accounts must be deposited within 1 month of approval (by 31 July for calendar-year filers)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Registry closure (cierre registral) blocking all further registrable acts and issuance of negative certificates; administrative fine under Ley 14/2013, art. 40 of EUR 1,200 to EUR 12,000 for late or non-filing; failure to deposit accounts for 3 consecutive years triggers strike-off and closure of the registry folio

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income Tax Return (Impuesto sobre Sociedades, Modelo 200), including the company's tax basis, deductions, and balance-sheet information
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months and 25 days after the fiscal year-end; for calendar-year taxpayers, annually by 25 July
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing surcharge of 5% to 20% of the assessed amount plus 3.75% annual late-payment interest; non-filing after formal demand carries a minimum base penalty of EUR 1,000 and proceeds under the tax enforcement regime; prolonged delinquency can lead to administrative seizure of assets and company strike-off in severe cases

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Information Return of Transactions with Third Parties (Declaración informativa anual de operaciones con terceras personas, Modelo 415), mandatory only if transactions with any single third party exceed EUR 3,005.06 in the fiscal year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Filing window from 1 February through the last calendar day of February following the reported fiscal year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing constitutes a tax infraction under Ley 58/2003 (LGT): base fine of EUR 200 per omitted return plus 1% of the undeclared transaction volume, subject to a EUR 1,000 minimum per undeclared counterparty; incorrect or incomplete filings carry an increased penalty of EUR 750 per return

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: UBO Annual Identity Confirmation (Declaración de Identificación del Titular Real) under Order JUS/319/2018, filed as an annex to the annual accounts deposit and covering the company's shareholding structure and all beneficial owners
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registro Mercantil, with data transmitted to the Registro Central de Titularidad Real (Spanish Central Beneficial Ownership Register, Ministry of Justice)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Fiscal year-end plus 7 months (31 July for calendar-year filers) as annexed to the annual accounts; any share transfer or UBO change must be recorded in the Libro Registro de Socios and separately declared to the Mercantile Registry within 10 business days of the notarized corporate deed
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Registry closure preventing registration of share transfers and other deeds; administrative fines under Ley 10/2010 up to EUR 60,000 for continuous non-declaration or misdeclaration of ultimate beneficial ownership; cross-referencing may trigger administrative dissolution inquiry for non-compliant dormant entities

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit under Ley de Auditoría de Cuentas 22/2015 and art. 263 Ley de Sociedades de Capital if at least two of three criteria are met for two consecutive fiscal years: balance sheet total exceeds EUR 2,850,000; net annual turnover exceeds EUR 5,700,000; average number of employees exceeds 50. Audit is also mandatory for entities issuing listed securities, receiving consolidated group treatment, or operating in insurance, reinsurance, or other regulated sectors. A POD custom-apparel SL operating below all thresholds qualifies for the small-company audit exemption.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Spanish GAAP (Plan General de Contabilidad) approved by Royal Decree 1514/2007 as amended by Royal Decree 1/2021; the abbreviated PGC-Pymes is available to qualifying small companies; consolidated groups must apply IFRS as endorsed by the European Union under Royal Decree 1159/2010

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The annual deposit of accounts operates as the company's yearly UBO confirmation: the Mercantile Registry's UBO declaration, filed with the Cuentas Anuales, must identify every individual who directly or indirectly owns or controls more than 25% of the share capital or voting rights, or who controls the company by other means. Any share transfer must first be entered in the Libro Registro de Socios, and the resulting change in beneficial ownership must be declared to the Registro Mercantil within 10 business days of formalization. The registrar then transmits updated UBO records to Spain's Registro Central de Titularidad Real under Ley 6/2023.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (Libro Registro de Socios)
Register of Directors (Libro Registro de Administradores)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: US$700–1,300 per year (EUR 600–1,100) for Spanish registered-office service and corporate secretarial agent support
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: US$2,500–5,500 (EUR 2,200–4,800) for a certified audit of a small to mid-size POD retail SL; companies below audit thresholds incur no audit cost

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: 15% reduced rate for newly created entities during the first two tax periods with a positive tax base; research and development and technological innovation tax credits (17%/10%); employment-generation deductions for income from certain intangible assets; regional tax adjustments in force.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Unlimited (statutory carry-forward without temporal expiry; offset may be quantitatively limited for large-turnover entities)

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Modelo 200 – Annual Corporate Income Tax Return filed electronically via the AEAT Sede Electrónica (tax agency e-office); advance payments are filed on Modelo 202/222.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual return; quarterly advance payments (payments on 20 April, 20 October, and 20 December for calendar-year taxpayers).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Filing must occur within 25 days following the six-month statutory period after the tax-year end; for a 31 December fiscal year-end, the deadline is 25 July of the following year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxpayer identification: NIF, legal name, registered address, ISIC activity code, and representative details
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For non-resident owners without local presence, include the tax representative's NIF and the related IRNR reference number where applicable.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Accounting profit or loss per the statutory income statement required under the General Chart of Accounts.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Spanish FRS-compliant financial statements of the SL are required; foreign-source entities piggybacking on the SL structure should align books to local GAAP.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Permanent and temporary differences, exclusions, and offset of prior tax-loss carryforwards
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholders claiming treaty or parent-subsidiary exemptions must ensure no non-resident deduction breaks are erroneously booked as local adjustments.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable base after statutory adjustments; application of 25% rate; tax credits and prepayments to compute final tax payable
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For non-resident controlled entities, review OECD TP and Spanish CFC rules before applying this amount to distribution or credit calculations.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing surcharge under Article 27 of Law 58/2003: 5% if filed within 3 months, 10% within 3–6 months, 15% within 6–12 months, and 20% thereafter, plus late-interest accrual. Unjustified non-filing may attract fixed assessment penalties and economic-administrative fines; fraudulent filings trigger criminal tax prosecution.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency_optional_validation: Quarterly advance payments filed on Form 202/222 do not replace the annual Modelo 200 obligation.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 19% Spanish non-resident income tax (IRNR) on distributions of profits from an SL to non-resident shareholders; rate may be reduced under an applicable tax treaty or exempted under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive for qualifying corporate shareholders that hold at least 10% of capital.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The beneficial owner must obtain a valid Certificate of Tax Residence (TRC) from the counterparty treaty jurisdiction and submit it to the Spanish payer before the income date. The payer then applies the treaty-reduced rate at source. In case of over-withholding, a refund must be claimed via Modelo 210 within the four-year statute of limitations. Annual disclosure of payments to non-residents is made on Modelo 296.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Spanish statutory rates: interest at 19% IRNR, royalties at 24% IRNR. Treaty relief usually lowers royalty rates to 10–15% and interest to 0–10% depending on the applicable agreement; domestic withholding law supersedes treaties only when more favorable to the taxpayer unless anti-abuse rules apply.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EUR 250,000 aggregate related-party transactions with a single related party per fiscal year triggers the documentation obligation (Local File, Form 232 information return). Master File is mandatory when the multinational group's consolidated annual revenue reaches EUR 45 million; Country-by-Country reporting applies at the EUR 750 million group-transaction threshold.
approved_arm_length_methodologies: CUP, Resale Price, Cost Plus, TNMM, Profit Split
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Spain does not employ UAE-style binary Economic Substance Regulations, but applies substantive tax-residency requirements (place of incorporation and effective management), OECD MLI substance-over-form rules, GAAR re-characterisation, CFC rules, and EU ATAD shell-entity measures. A Spanish SL lacking real employees, premises, and operational activity is vulnerable to treaty denial and administrative re-location.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Knowingly omitting POD platform sales, using dual or secret e-commerce ledgers, or fabricating deductible invoices for nonexistent printing services
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Economic-administrative surcharge of 50%–100% of the omitted tax amount plus late interest; criminal tax offence if fraud quota exceeds EUR 120,000 per year, carrying up to six years imprisonment and fines of up to six times the defrauded amount.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who consented to or facilitated the false filing are jointly and severally liable for the tax debt and civil restitution; the court may impose director travel bans and disqualification from holding public contracts or receiving subsidies.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Sham Substance and Treaty Abuse
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the SL as an empty vehicle to route E-commerce royalties and dividends through Spain solely to claim Spanish treaty network benefits or avoid strict substance rules in the beneficial-owner jurisdiction
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of treaty benefits, recharacterization of artificial interposed entities, and re-assessed non-resident withholding tax with surcharges; Spanish GAAR may impose a 50% penalty on the under-declared tax base; criminal exposure for intentional misstatement.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be personally assessed for unpaid withholding tax and for unjustified tax benefits; courts may freeze personal assets and block exit from the jurisdiction during the criminal inquiry.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Charging uncommercial markups for SL's POD fulfilment, logistics, or advisory contracts with non-resident affiliates and failing to file the Form 232 related-party information return
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Adjusted taxable base plus late interest; TP documentation deficiencies are finable per data set or control book, and inaccurate or incomplete documentation can trigger a penalty of 1%–10% of the value of connected transactions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors of the managing entity may be held jointly liable when they intentionally used unsubstantiated prices to erode Spanish taxable base; professional-advisory fees may also be attacked in subsequent claw-back claims.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Channeling Stripe/PayPal receivables into inaccessible offshore accounts or accepting payments from high-risk counterparties without any compliance review
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Financial penalties under Spain's AML Law (Law 10/2010) that range from EUR 150,000 in serious cases up to ten times the benefit obtained, including suspension of legal activity; failure to identify beneficial owners can trigger separate administrative sanctions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors with actual or legal control over the payment infrastructure can be personally sanctioned for AML governance failures; criminal courts may order travel restrictions, seizure of personal and corporate bank accounts, and imprisonment in laundering schemes.
